title: WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert, players to discuss growing online harassment problem
content:
NEW YORK — Women’s National Basketball Players Association leaders are set to meet with league leadership, including commissioner Cathy Engelbert, to discuss online harassment players have been increasingly subject to in recent weeks.

The meeting, scheduled for Tuesday, will include the WNBPA’s executive committee as well as the Justice, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion Committee.

“It’s literally a temperature check of everything from the first half of the season,” said New York Liberty forward Breanna Stewart, the WNBPA vice president. “The security and the negative effects from sports betting is really hitting home for a lot of people and definitely not what you want. But it happens when the sport gets bigger and bigger.”

The meeting was initiated by player leadership, WNBPA secretary and Chicago Sky center Elizabeth Williams told The Athletic, following a controversial play between Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark and Phoenix Mercury forward Alyssa Thomas. Williams said outreach was made before the league decided to issue Thomas a one-game suspension.

Williams said players don’t have a full agenda for the upcoming meeting, but one of the goals is to address league leadership’s need to be more proactive versus reactive in times of crisis.

“Things are always addressed after the fact,” Williams said. “It takes controversy or a little bit of heat before statements are made or before things are addressed. Early on when (Engelbert) first joined, she was a little bit more proactive and that helped build her relationship with players. And now it doesn’t necessarily feel that way.”

In the aftermath of the play between Clark and Thomas, which was retroactively upgraded to a flagrant 2 penalty, Thomas said she and her family received online death threats and harassment, including racial slurs. Her partner and teammate, DeWanna Bonner, shared some of the death threats she received with The Athletic, which included addresses associated with her and her family as well as personal phone numbers. At the time, Bonner said she had not spoken to Engelbert in years.

Engelbert issued a statement after Thomas publicly addressed the league’s silence and criticized Engelbert, saying she “vehemently condemns any and all forms of hate.” As a speaker on a panel Thursday in New York, Engelbert called such online vitriol “unacceptable” and broadly talked about WNBA security measures.

Bonner is part of the JEDI committee and is expected to participate in Tuesday’s meeting.

In recent weeks, more players have exposed the threats and bigotry they’ve received online. Las Vegas Aces guard Chelsea Gray shared a screenshot of an Instagram direct message she received that included a racial slur. She shared an accompanying message with the screenshot that said, “People act like we just make this s— up. And the audacity to tell us as athletes to ‘shut up and dribble.’”

Gray later told reporters why she decided to share the message. “These messages are not the first of its kind. There was other stuff too. I just decided to share that one. It was just time.”
